headline: Public Beach Access and Backroad Navigation
reservation: Day-use at the main public beach in Harrison Hot Springs does not require a permit, but parking is strictly regulated during summer months. Commercial hot springs access is typically limited to resort guests or specific spa bookings; check current public pool availability through the village office.

days.title: Lakeside Vistas and Village Life

stops.name: Harrison Lagoon
stops.detail: Walk the scenic promenade for a view of the floating water park and the surrounding mountains.

stops.name: Spirit Trail
stops.detail: Explore a local cedar forest adorned with traditional masks carved into the trees.

days.driving: Minimal; local village areas are walkable from central parking.
days.note: Weekend crowds in the village can significantly increase travel time between local sights.

days.title: Eastern Shore Adventure

stops.name: Sasquatch Provincial Park
stops.detail: Visit Hicks Lake or Deer Lake for quiet water activities away from the main resort area.

stops.name: Green Point
stops.detail: A popular day-use spot for picnicking and viewing the expansive northern reach of the lake.

days.driving: Allow 1 hour for the winding roads into the provincial park area; conditions vary.
days.note: Provincial park gates typically close at dusk; check posted seasonal hours.

days.title: River Confluence and History
days.start: Suggested: 9:30 AM from Harrison Hot Springs

stops.name: Kilby Historic Site
stops.detail: A short drive to Harrison Mills to explore a 1920s general store and farm near the Harrison River.

stops.name: Sandalwood Falls
stops.detail: Observe the seasonal cascades located along the nearby forest service roads.

days.driving: Allow 1.5 hours for the return trip to Harrison Mills and local forest road segments.
days.note: Forest service roads may be rough; high clearance is advised for falls access.

intel.title: Village and Park Congestion
intel.text: Paid parking is in effect throughout the Harrison Village core. Sasquatch Provincial Park lots often reach capacity by mid-morning on sunny summer weekends.

intel.title: Variable Mountain Coverage
intel.text: Cellular reception is strong in Harrison Hot Springs and Agassiz but drops off quickly when traveling north along the forest service roads or deeper into Sasquatch Park.

intel.title: Fraser Valley Supply Points
intel.text: Major fuel stations are located in Agassiz and Chilliwack. There is no fuel available along the remote East or West Harrison Forest Service Roads.

intel.title: Seasonal Water Levels
intel.text: Lake levels fluctuate significantly with spring snowmelt; beach sizes at Green Point and the village may vary. Boat launches can be impacted by these seasonal changes.

intel.title: Forest Service Road Status
intel.text: The West Harrison FSR is a rugged industrial road; check for active logging activity and washouts before attempting to reach the northern end of the lake.

plan.arrival: Arrive via Abbotsford (YXX), drive north through Agassiz, and secure supplies in the village before heading to provincial park sites.
plan.vehicle: Standard vehicles are fine for the village and Sasquatch Provincial Park; 4WD with high clearance is required for the Harrison Forest Service Roads.
plan.goldenHour: Sunset from the Harrison Lake public docks, looking north toward the Douglas Ranges.
